subject: School Override Spending and Inclusion Initiatives
overview: School Committee Vice Chair Jenny Graham and parent advocate Patricia Chery discussed the implementation of $7 million in override funding, highlighting staff retention and new special education programs. The district approved several immediate investments in technology, infrastructure, and inclusion while preparing for long-term schedule changes.

items.title: Allocation of Override Revenue
items.summary: The School Committee unanimously approved an administration proposal to spend $5.25 million of the $7 million override revenue available in the current fiscal year.

items.title: Staff Retention and Technology Budget
items.summary: The override funding permanently saved 14 positions that were previously at risk of elimination and established a recurring $500,000 budget for technology replacements.

items.title: Inclusion and Special Education Programming
items.summary: Following advocacy from parents, the district approved the launch of a Best Buddies program at the high school, the hiring of an inclusion specialist, and increased bus monitoring.

items.title: Operational Support and Capital Repairs
items.summary: Approved investments include a third payroll specialist, swing-shift custodians, high school elevator repairs, and roofing fixes for McGlynn Elementary School.

items.title: Future Schedule and Contract Negotiations
items.summary: The district is currently negotiating with bargaining units to use $3.7 million in remaining funds for longer school days and high school schedule restructuring for the next academic year.
